posts.content_md:
Has anyone tried to coat plate with emulsion using some type of spray system? I was thinking an air brush (for paints) may be used if they came with a nozzle that prayed a thin wide area. Then a glass plate could be placed on a continuous feed belt and upon varying the speed of the belt, one could obtain different and precisely reproduceable unifom emulsion thicknesses that go to the edge of the plate.

If anyone has tried this method with success, what type of spray system was used.

Thank you,

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md: There was a paper by a German group two or three years ago (2003?)in SPIE. They were coating a continuous roll with a large pipe across the roll with several holes in it. The gel was forced through the holes as the roll was fed underneath. The paper is at work and I'm at home so I don't have title and paper. Unless someone can come up with it in the next few hours, I'll post it then. They seem to have good coating success.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
The latest paper I am reading states, "The DCG-layers were coated by a nozzle deposition technique onto glass substrates."

Influence of the dichromate concentration on the

holographic properties of dichromated gelatin layers

J. Schulat, K. Fröhlich, C.G. Stojanoff*

That's why I am thinking spray, but I have worked with air brushing and I don't think it will do large format. I may try an electric paint sprayer that sprays in a fan profile. Going up to Home Depot today to see what I can find.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md: i was always suspect that Lee Lacey spray coated his plates. i tried it using the basic formula ,10-30-200 and i kept thinning the solution with iso alch until it sprayed out of the persval sprayer ..... the results were good, but i wasn't to happy atomizing toxic particulate everywhere. it is possible to spray-on gelatine first, then harden the plates via vapor method ,then dip in a AmDi solution. Lee Lacey is a fantastic dcg holographer , i was lucky enough to work with in the mid 80s.......
